findings.stopName: Šćepan Polje → Piva Canyon drive (via Plužine)
findings.claimChecked: note/route assume a clean morning drive down to the Šćepan Polje raft start and an afternoon Piva-canyon drive
findings.finding: VERIFIED 2026 roadworks: multiple current Bosnian traffic bulletins report works on the Brod na Drini (Foča)–Hum (Šćepan Polje) road — exactly the Day-7 morning approach to the raft start — with slow driving and temporary ~10-minute traffic stops. The Plužine–Šćepan Polje (Piva canyon) leg also has an active WBIF reconstruction underway. Neither is a full closure, but both add buffer time and the canyon road is narrow/tunnelled.
findings.recommendedAction: Add to the drive note: 'Roadworks on Foča→Hum (Šćepan Polje) in 2026 = slow driving + temporary ~10-min stops; add 20-30min buffer for the morning leg to the raft start.' Leave Pale earlier accordingly.

skeptic.claim: Day-7 morning approach to the Šćepan Polje raft start (Brod na Drini/Foča–Hum road) has active 2026 roadworks with slow driving and ~10-min temporary traffic stops (not a closure); the Plužine–Šćepan Polje Piva-canyon leg also has an active WBIF reconstruction underway.
skeptic.evidence: Independently confirmed the core, plan-relevant claim. A separate outlet (srpskainfo.com) mirroring the same Republika Srpska road-authority traffic bulletin, dated June 2, 2026 (12 days pre-trip), explicitly lists "Brod na Drini (Foča)–Hum (Šćepan Polje)" with "se vozi usporeno sa privremenim prekidima u trajanju od 10 minuta" (slower driving, temporary 10-minute interruptions) — exactly the Day-7 morning approach to the raft start, and not a full closure. Multiple recurring 2026 bulletins repeat this. The cited glassrpske URL (634896) and its siblings return HTTP 403 to fetch but appear in search with the identical wording, and the live 636843 bulletin corroborates. HOWEVER, the first checker's SECONDARY claim — an "active WBIF reconstruction underway" on the Plužine–Šćepan Polje canyon leg — is overstated/inaccurate: federalna.ba (Dec 14, 2025) and corroborating sources state the WBIF/World Bank/EBRD project is still in the TENDER phase (two qualified bidders, contract expected end-2025), with works only "expected to start by mid-2026" and not yet physically underway on the canyon. The one section under active construction (investitor.me) is the separate Zaborje–Jasenovo Polje stretch on the Nikšić approach, finishing early 2026, not the Piva canyon road. The canyon being narrow/tunnelled (24 tunnels in ~20km) is independently true. Net: the practical Day-7 advice (buffer time on the morning approach, no closure) holds and is confirmed; the "active canyon reconstruction" detail should be corrected to "tender/planned, works expected mid-2026."

findings.claimChecked: bestTime says: 'Day 8 (Jun 23) — alternative Durmitor PLATEAU WALK if skipping Veliki Međed. Start by 07:00; no shelter on the open plateau if storms close in.'
findings.finding: The bestTime describes Prutaš as a gentle 'plateau walk' — but the NOTE and every source describe Prutaš as a steep, exposed, scrambly summit (UIAA-I, fixed cables, scree, sections of near-rock-climbing), NOT a plateau walk. The bestTime is leftover text from an earlier 'Veliki Međed' version of this slot and contradicts the note's own difficulty warning. Calling it a plateau walk dangerously understates the commitment.
findings.recommendedAction: Rewrite bestTime to match the note: 'Day 8 (Jun 23) — Prutaš is the conditions-dependent ★ summit, NOT a casual plateau walk: steep scramble (UIAA-I, cables, scree). Trailhead 06:00-06:30, off the ridge by noon (June PM storms, no shelter up high). Non-technical fallback = Planinica or Black Lake loop.'

skeptic.claim: The bestTime's "plateau walk" wording dangerously understates Prutaš, which (per the checker) the note and every source describe as a steep, exposed, scrambly UIAA-I summit with fixed cables and near-rock-climbing — leftover Veliki Međed text that contradicts the note's own difficulty warning.
skeptic.evidence: The finding's core premises are false. (1) The entry's NOTE field is empty (None) — there is no "note's own difficulty warning" to contradict; the checker fabricated it. (2) The UIAA-I / fixed-cables / scramble characterization belongs to VELIKI MEĐED, not Prutaš. The data file's own communityNotes say: "COMPARE WITH VELIKI MEĐED... that route has UIAA-I scrambling and fixed cables — much harder. Prutaš is the everyone-can-do-it choice." Independent searches confirm the fixed cables / scramble-down-rock-face in this area belong to Veliki Međed (Black Lake start) and the Durmitor via ferratas (Uvita Greda/Bobotov Kuk), NOT the Prutaš plateau route. The checker mis-attributed the other peak's difficulty to Prutaš — the inverse of the truth. (3) Independent sources agree Prutaš's standard summit route is moderate/plateau-like: Moon & Honey Travel calls it "a moderate and straightforward out-and-back day hike" across "wildflower-carpeted meadows" with a summit that is "a wide grassy plateau"; The Sandy Feet says difficulty "stems primarily from length and elevation change rather than technical climbing" and the summit "does not require hands." Serious scrambling/ropes only appear on the EXTENDED Prutaš→Škrčko Lake traverse or the harder Todorov Do western approach, not the standard Sedlo-pass summit-and-back the plan describes (9km, "no technical exposure"). The bestTime correctly says "alternative ... if skipping Veliki Međed," matching the description — it is NOT leftover Veliki Međed text. Minor caveat: sources do note "two rugged areas requiring light exposure" and "a short exposed section," so "plateau walk" is mildly optimistic — but vastly closer to truth than the checker's claim, and not dangerous or contradictory.

anchorPass.summary: This is a tight, taste-aware plan — most days lead with a nature/activity ★ (canyoning, bridge jump, Tara raft, Durmitor, kayaks, boat rentals) and the planner has already pre-demoted the obvious fat (Makarska nightlife, Mljet cave-OR-kayak, Skadar SUP, D13 Bellevue, Dubrovnik walls all carry explicit "skip/option" flags in their own notes). So I'm NOT padding the list. The genuinely weak committed stops cluster around sightseeing/monuments that survive in the itinerary as defaults rather than options: Krka (D1), Počitelj (D4), the Jablanica WWII museum (D6), Ostrog (D9), and Budva Old Town (D11) are the clearest taste-rule frictions. Ston Walls (D3, a ★) is the one debatable top-pick — a no-shade monument walk wedged onto the most time-fragile day. Mratinje Dam (D7) is low-payoff but nearly free on the road, so it's a softer flag. Net: the plan is strong; trim/demote these few and it gets tighter without losing a single big highlight. Note: I judged against the group's "nature+activity over sightseeing, dislike generic old towns/museums/monuments unless iconic-and-on-route" rule; coordinates and on-route logic check out across the file.

weakestStops.whyWeak: Worst payoff-for-cost on the trip for this group: ~77km-corridor inland NP where swimming has been BANNED since 2021, so it reduces to a paid boardwalk walk/photo at EUR40pp (EUR160 for 4) on a jet-lagged arrival day. That is exactly the 'sightseeing, no activity' the group dislikes, and the day already has its real water highlight (Skradin town beach swim, pick=true). Its own note calls it 'THE skip candidate.' It is committed (pick listed) rather than dropped, which is the weakness.
weakestStops.betterAlternative: none — keep the Skradin beach swim as the day's water; treat Krka as drop-by-default. If they want moving water on D1, the legal Krka swim already lives in the Skradin beach stop, so no new stop is needed.

weakestStops.whyWeak: A textbook taste violation: a 'bare stone hill, little shade' Ottoman old-town/fortress photo stop — generic-old-town sightseeing that is NOT iconic-on-route in the Mostar-bridge/Kotor-fortress sense. On a day already carrying two strong water ★ (Mljet kayak) plus Kravica falls, it is the redundant low-energy add (group will be hot and ferry-rushed).
weakestStops.betterAlternative: none — keep as an optional 5-min pomegranate-stall leg-stretch, not a committed 45-50min stop. The day is full; cutting it just adds slack, which the group values. (If they want one more swim, Kravica already covers water.)

weakestStops.stopName: Battle of Neretva Museum & sunken bridge (Jablanica)
weakestStops.whyWeak: Explicitly a WWII museum + monument — the single clearest hit against the 'dislike museums/monuments unless iconic' rule. It is on-route but not iconic to this young/adventurous group, and D6 is a long Sarajevo drive day where the real highlight (Baščaršija/Žuta sunset, pick=true) plus a Boračko Lake swim already fill the slack better.
weakestStops.betterAlternative: Boračko Lake (ba-boracko-lake, already on the same day's drive ~16km from Konjic) — a glacial-lake swim + self-rent rowboat/pedalo is a strictly better on-route break than a museum for this group. Lead the morning with that and let the museum be a 10-min drive-by photo of the sunken bridge only.

weakestStops.whyWeak: A religious monument requiring covered knees/shoulders, no photos in prayer rooms, pilgrim-bus crowds — sightseeing, not nature/activity. It is roughly on the Žabljak→Skadar line and is the region's signature sight, so it is borderline-iconic, but for this group it is the day's weakest item and its own note already tags it 'the day's drop candidate.' Eats a real 2:11 mountain-drive morning before the D9 ★ kayak.
weakestStops.betterAlternative: none — keep as a short 30-45min facade/cliff-setting stop (the cliff-embedded architecture is the genuinely striking part) and protect the time for the Crnojevića kayak + Pavlova Strana. Don't expand it.

weakestStops.whyWeak: Generic walled old town the group will only 'quick stop' — they base in Stoliv and do the Kotor bar night, not Budva nightlife, so the old town itself adds little. D11 already has the real highlights (Sveti Nikola cliff-jumping, Kotor fortress ★, optional Kotor bay kayak). With the Vrmac-tunnel roadworks buffer warning on this very stop, time spent in Budva old town directly threatens the ~17:00 Kotor fortress sunset.
weakestStops.betterAlternative: Sveti Nikola Island ('Hawaii') cliff-jumping + swim (me-sveti-nikola-island, same morning, same zone) — make that the Budva-area activity and reduce the old town to a parking-and-a-walk-through. That protects the drive buffer to Kotor and fits taste far better.

weakestStops.whyWeak: The one debatable ★ top-pick: a no-shade limestone monument-wall walk (EUR10pp) wedged into the most time-fragile day in the plan (D3 = airport pickup + last-ferry SPOF). It is a sightseeing climb, not nature/activity, and any overrun cascades into the 20:30 ferry risk flagged on the same day. Iconic-ish but a stretch for the taste rule, and the schedule cost is real.
weakestStops.betterAlternative: none structurally, but de-star it: do the shortest Ston→Mali Ston traverse only (already noted) or drop it entirely if the morning runs late, leaning on Mali Ston oysters as the on-route Pelješac stop. Should be a flex/skip item, not a ★ anchor on the SPOF day.

weakestStops.whyWeak: A 'roadside photo stop, exposed concrete, no shade — don't linger' sight on a day that is already a strong activity day (Tara raft ★) plus genuine scenery (Piva Lake swim/kayak, the 56-tunnel canyon drive). Low payoff and pure sightseeing, though its cost is small since it's directly on the road south.
weakestStops.betterAlternative: none — keep as a 10-min drive-by, not a 25-min stop; the Piva Lake turquoise swim (me-piva-lake-swim, same day, same road) is the superior and self-rentable on-route stop and already in the plan. This is the softest flag of the set.

The fortress and old town will be unusually calm all day — the plan's me-kotor 'cruise tourists arrive ~09:30' / forced-early logic does not apply Jun 26. Keep the ~17:00 golden-hour climb (heat is the real reason to go late, not crowds), but you are FREE to also wander the old town midday without the usual cruise crush. Update the me-kotor note so the group doesn't needlessly rush.
changes.why: cruisetimetables.com Kotor June 2026 calendar: Jun 26 has no scheduled calls; Jun 25 had Azamara Onward, Mein Schiff 4, MSC Armonia, Norwegian Pearl. The committed note assumes cruise crowding that isn't there on this specific date.

changes.suggestion: Add a date-specific nightlife anchor: Jun 21 2026 is the OPENING night of the Garden of Dreams electronic-music festival (multi-venue across Sarajevo, parties run late ~22:00+) AND the opening day of Summer in the Park – Hastahana (Marijin Dvor beer-garden with live music, runs all summer). This squarely fits the group's nightlife/electronic taste and lands exactly on their Sarajevo overnight. Note it on ba-bascarsija-bar-cluster as the headline option for the night, and verify the 2026 lineup/venue/ticket on sarajevo.travel a few days ahead (the detailed lineup I found was a cached prior edition).
changes.why: sarajevo.travel 'Top events June 20-26' lists Garden of Dreams (electronic, multi-venue) and Summer in the Park–Hastahana both opening Jun 21. A real festival on the exact overnight date is higher-value than a generic bar crawl for this group, and the sober-driver constraint already in the plan still applies.

Explorer of the Seas (3,114 pax) arrives Gruž at 10:00 on Jun 28 — the Old Town walls/Stradun will be at peak crush from ~10:30. If anyone wants the walls or Old Town, do it 08:00-09:30 and be out before 10:30; otherwise lead the day purely on the 10:00 sea-kayak (already the pick) and skip the Old Town. This also reinforces the existing 18:00 Old-Town-leave rule: Gruž cruise traffic + cruise-day road load is exactly why Old Town->Čilipi can run 45-60min. changes.why: cruisetimetables.com Dubrovnik Jun 28 2026: Explorer of the Seas 3,114 pax arr 10:00 dep 20:00, plus Star Clipper. Confirms — with a specific ship/time — the plan's general cruise-day caution; an 08:00 walls slot is the only comfortable window.

changes.suggestion: Re-sequence the D5 morning so the Stari Most jump truly lands first and cool. The committed picks have ba-mostar-bridge-jump (★, ~09:00) and ba-blagaj (midday ~13:00), but ba-mostar's note still carries a contradictory 'arrive late afternoon from Kravica / sunset' bestTime line, and ba-fortica's bestTime says 'morning.' For late June 35C+ heat, lock the order to: Stari Most jump + cevapi 09:00-11:00 (cool, empty) -> Blagaj Tekija + icy Buna swim + Vrelo trout 12:30-15:00 (midday heat-relief on cold karst water) -> Fortica skywalk/zipline 16:00-18:00 (exposed but heat eased) -> Drežnica canyon swim on the drive N. Clean up the stale bestTime strings so the morning-vs-afternoon is unambiguous.
changes.why: The picks are right but residual bestTime fields contradict the chosen order (some say sunset/afternoon Mostar, some say morning Fortica). On these hot dates the jump and old town MUST be the cool-morning block and the exposed Fortica hilltop the late-afternoon block; the cold Buna swim is the correct midday heat sink.

changes.suggestion: Make the late-arrival Krka decision date-honest. With a 10:00 Zadar car pickup and the full Zadar->Krvavica drive, you realistically reach Krka mid/late afternoon. Lean into the after-15:00 ticket (EUR30pp vs EUR40pp) the plan already flags, but add the local move: enter from the SKRADIN side (not Lozovac), park in Skradin, and walk/boat in — that way Skradin town beach swim (the legal swim, already the D1 ★) needs no separate boat hop and you skip the Lozovac bus queue. If energy is low, skip the falls entirely and just do the Skradin beach swim + camp at Krvavica with daylight. Note-only tightening of hr-krka / hr-skradin-town-beach.
changes.why: hr-krka already notes the EUR30 after-15:00 window and online-timed entry; the Skradin-side entry is the local trick that merges the paid park visit with the free legal swim and avoids the Lozovac shuttle bottleneck on a tired arrival afternoon.

changes.suggestion: Flag the June water-lily bloom as a real timing payoff on the Crnojevića river. Lake Skadar / Rijeka Crnojevića water lilies and lush channel greenery peak in early summer and the lake sits ~26C (warm swim). For the D9 self-rent kayak and Pavlova Strana viewpoint, paddle the channel in the morning calm (operator wind rule + lily visibility both favor AM) and shoot Pavlova Strana in late-afternoon golden light as planned. Add a one-line note to me-skadar-rijeka-crnojevica-kayak that late June is peak lily season on the channel — a genuine this-window bonus, not generic.
changes.why: Montenegro Skadar sources confirm summer lake ~26C and water-lily cover; the bloom is a specific June visual that rewards the morning channel paddle the plan already schedules. Pure upside, no schedule change.

changes.suggestion: Keep the Prutaš pick but make the snow fallback explicit for late June. Verified: snow lingers on Durmitor's higher/exposed ridges into late June, and the Prutaš upper section (UIAA-I, cables) is exactly where it holds. The plan's me-prutas-hike already says 'conditions-dependent' — strengthen it to a hard decision gate: ask the Boričje host on the D7 night AND check the AM sky; if snow/storm risk, default to the Black Lake loop or Planinica (both snow-free, no scramble) rather than improvising at the trailhead. This protects the group-taste 'one big highlight' without a sketchy ridge.
changes.why: Multiple Durmitor hiking sources confirm late-June snow patches at elevation; Prutaš's cabled upper ridge is the icing-prone part. Afternoon storms are typical in June, reinforcing the off-ridge-by-noon rule already noted. Fallbacks must be pre-decided, not gambled.

changes.suggestion: Pre-buy the Prapratno->Sobra ferry ticket online NOW and treat the 20:30 as Plan A only if clearing arrivals by ~17:50. Re-confirmed for the Jun 18 window: 20:30 is the last sailing, cars first-come (~50/boat, no reservation of the slot), queue 45-60min in peak season. The single highest-fragility moment of the trip. The online pre-buy only skips the desk — it does NOT guarantee a car space — so the real safeguard is the mainland Plan B (sleep near Ston, take 07:00/10:15 ferry D4). Make sure the to-do has the pre-buy as a do-now item, not a book-on-the-road item.
changes.why: Jadrolinija/croatiaferries confirm 20:30 last sailing + 45-60min peak queue; a delayed 17:20 friend landing can blow the window. The plan flags this as the #1 SPOF — the date-specific action is buy online now AND keep the mainland fallback booked-able, because a delayed flight on this exact evening is the realistic failure mode.

changes.suggestion: Verify the summer-2026 Budva->Kotor roadworks status a day or two ahead and pre-plan the Trojica bypass. The plan's me-budva note warns Vrmac-tunnel + Tivat-Jaz roadworks can triple the drive to 60-90min — this is a live 2026 construction situation, so check current status (Google Maps live + a quick local-forum/news check) on D10 evening. If the Vrmac tunnel shows dark-red Jun 26, take the Trojica switchback turn-off (~20min faster) and leave Budva by ~15:00 to hold the ~17:00 fortress sunset. Since Jun 26 has no Kotor cruise ships, you have more midday slack to absorb a slow transfer than the note assumes.
changes.why: The committed note already names the Vrmac/Tivat-Jaz roadworks as a 2026 hazard; roadwork status changes month to month, so it must be re-verified on the day. Combined with the zero-cruise Jun 26 finding, the group has more buffer than the worst-case note implies.
